headline: 16 contracts catalogued across Solana (2 programs, 2 tokens), EVM (12 pool contracts across 2 pools), and Stellar (10 contracts); Solana program IDs are base58 and cannot populate 0x admin_addresses directly.

findings.text: D1: Solana does not have an Etherscan-style name-tag search endpoint. No EVM block-explorer search performed for Solana chain. Solana program addresses discovered via docs (D2) instead. Recorded as D1-offchain fallback.

D2: Official deployed-contracts page at docs.huma.finance/ecosystem-resources/smart-contracts lists 2 Solana program addresses (Huma, Huma Institutional), 2 Solana SPL token mints (PST, mPST), 12 EVM addresses across two Arf pools (Arf 3-month and Arf 6-month), and 10 Stellar contract addresses. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set accordingly.

D3: Audit page at docs.huma.finance/ecosystem-resources/security-audits lists 9 audit reports: Halborn (Huma 2.0 Solana programs + 2 incremental), Sec3 (Huma Prime + 3 incremental), Spearbit (2 EVM reports), Certora (Stellar). No in-scope contract address table was accessible from the audit page itself — linked PDFs/Halborn pages not fetched due to tool budget. Audit firms and report URLs recorded.

D4: GitHub org 00labs confirmed via search, with repos including huma-contracts-v2, huma-signals, huma-utils, governance-ui, distributor, permissionless-sdk-example. No pinned commit SHA fetched due to tool call budget. GitHub URLs added to protocol_metadata.github.

D5: protocol.chains lists only Solana, but docs show EVM (likely Polygon, consistent with V1 context and Arf pools) and Stellar deployments also present. EVM chain for the Arf pool contracts was not confirmed on-chain in this run — recorded in unknowns.

D6: No factory-pattern contracts identified on Solana from docs. Stellar ContractFactory address surfaced but factory children not enumerated (Stellar not supported by DeFiPunkd read API). EVM Arf pools appear to be individually-listed, not factory-discovered.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: Solana program addresses classified as 'other' (programs, not admin keys); EVM pool contracts classified as 'pool' and 'vault' roles; Stellar contracts classified by role label from docs.

D8: All admin_addresses entries trace to the fetched docs URL at docs.huma.finance/ecosystem-resources/smart-contracts. Solana base58 program IDs and Stellar addresses do not conform to 0x format and cannot be placed in admin_addresses[]; recorded in unknowns with D8 code.

rationale.verdict: Walked official docs (security-audits + smart-contracts pages), website, and GitHub org search. Catalogued 16 deployed entities: 2 Solana programs, 2 Solana SPL mints, 12 EVM pool contracts (2 Arf pools × 6 contracts each), and 10 Stellar contracts. Solana program IDs are base58-encoded and Stellar addresses are Strkey-encoded — neither fits the 0x admin_addresses schema; EVM pool contract addresses are populated where the 0x format applies. On-chain verification of EVM chain ID and Solana program authority keys remains for next slice.

protocol_metadata.about: Huma Finance V2 is a permissionless PayFi (Payment Finance) network built natively on Solana that enables liquidity providers to deposit USDC and earn real-world yield from global payment financing activities such as cross-border payments, trade finance, and payroll advances. Users receive PST (PayFi Strategy Token), a liquid yield-bearing SPL token that can be used across the Solana DeFi ecosystem via integrations with Jupiter, Kamino, and RateX. The protocol operates through Solana programs secured by multisigs, with yield generated from daily financing fees paid by businesses accessing on-chain liquidity — not from token emissions or speculation. Huma Institutional is a parallel permissioned product for accredited investors, with EVM deployments on Polygon for legacy Arf pools.
